title: B.Tech admissions 2026: eligibility and entrance test
text: For the B.Tech batch starting in July 2026, applicants must have passed class twelve with Physics and Mathematics as compulsory subjects, along with one of Chemistry, Computer Science or Biotechnology. They need at least 60 percent aggregate in Physics, Mathematics and the best of the third subject; the minimum is 55 percent for SC, ST and OBC non-creamy layer candidates of the state. Students awaiting class twelve results may apply and take the test, but admission is confirmed only when the marksheet is submitted. The university's Admission Aptitude Test (AAT) is compulsory for all B.Tech applicants. Scores from national or state engineering entrance examinations are not accepted in place of the AAT, although they may be listed on the form for information. The AAT is a 150-minute computer-based test with 120 questions in Mathematics, Physics and logical reasoning, with negative marking of one quarter mark. Seats in each branch are filled in order of AAT rank, subject to the eligibility marks above. Candidates may take the AAT in both admission rounds; the better score is used.

title: BBA, B.Com and BA admissions 2026: eligibility
text: For the BBA, B.Com (Honours) and BA programmes starting in July 2026, applicants need to have passed class twelve in any stream with at least 50 percent aggregate, or 45 percent for SC, ST and OBC non-creamy layer candidates of the state. B.Com (Honours) additionally needs Mathematics or Accountancy in class twelve. There is no entrance test for these programmes: admission is on the basis of class twelve marks. BBA applicants are shortlisted on marks and then attend a 15-minute personal interview, held on campus or online. BA applicants choose their major in the second semester, not at admission. Students who took a gap year after class twelve must submit a gap affidavit on stamp paper explaining the gap. Lateral entry is not available for these programmes, and students cannot switch from a BA to a BBA after the first semester. The application fee and round dates are the same as for B.Tech, and the same refund rules apply after admission.

title: MBA admissions 2026: eligibility and selection
text: The two-year MBA programme starting in July 2026 is open to graduates in any discipline with at least 50 percent aggregate marks, or 45 percent for reserved category candidates of the state. Final-year students are not eligible: the degree must be completed, with results declared, by the last date of the round in which the candidate applies. Candidates need either an AAT management score or a valid national management entrance test score from the last two years. Shortlisted candidates attend a group discussion and a personal interview on campus. The composite score used for the merit list is made up of the entrance test score 50 percent, personal interview 25 percent, group discussion 15 percent, and work experience 10 percent. Work experience is counted in full months after graduation, with 1 mark per completed 6 months up to a maximum of 10 marks; internships do not count. The intake is 120 seats, of which 15 percent are reserved for candidates with at least 2 years of full-time work experience.

title: Admission rounds and application fee, 2026 intake
text: Applications for the July 2026 intake are accepted in three rounds. Round 1: applications close on 15 March 2026, the AAT is held on 5 April 2026, and results are published on 20 April. Round 2: applications close on 10 May 2026, the AAT is held on 31 May 2026, and results are published on 12 June. Round 3 is a spot round on 30 June 2026 for vacant seats only, open to candidates who already hold an AAT score from round 1 or 2. The application fee is ₹1,200 per programme, or ₹600 for SC and ST candidates. A combined form for up to three programmes costs ₹1,800, or ₹900 for SC and ST candidates. The application fee is not refundable, including when a candidate is found ineligible. Edits to a submitted form, such as changing the test city, are allowed once, until 48 hours before the round closes. This schedule replaces the two-round schedule used for the 2025 intake.

title: Admission rounds and application fee, 2025 intake (superseded)
text: This schedule for the July 2025 intake is superseded by the three-round schedule for the 2026 intake and is kept only for reference. In 2025 there were two rounds. Round 1 applications closed on 31 March 2025 with the AAT on 20 April 2025, and round 2 applications closed on 31 May 2025 with the AAT on 15 June 2025. There was no spot round; vacant seats were offered from the round 2 waiting list. The application fee was ₹1,000 per programme, or ₹500 for SC and ST candidates, and there was no combined form for several programmes. Candidates applying to more than one programme paid the full fee for each. Corrections to submitted forms could be requested by email until the round closed. Results were sent by post as well as being published online, and admitted students had 10 days to pay the first instalment of fees.

title: Tuition fees and payment rules, 2026 batch
text: B.Tech tuition for students admitted in 2026 is ₹1,85,000 per year, BBA ₹1,10,000 per year, B.Com (Honours) ₹78,000 per year, BA ₹52,000 per year, and MBA ₹2,60,000 per year. Tuition is fixed at admission: the yearly tuition fee will not change for the batch until the normal duration of the programme ends, so a 2026 B.Tech student pays ₹1,85,000 in every one of the four years. Students who need extra semesters beyond the normal duration pay the fee applicable to the batch then running. A one-time admission fee of ₹25,000 is paid with the first instalment. Tuition is paid in two equal instalments each year, due on 15 July and 15 January. A late fee of ₹100 per day is charged after the due date, up to a maximum of ₹5,000. If fees are still unpaid 30 days after the due date, the student's name is struck off the rolls and re-admission needs the Registrar's approval and a re-admission fee of ₹2,500.

title: Merit scholarships and sibling concession, 2026 batch onwards
text: Merit scholarships for students admitted from 2026 are a waiver of tuition fee only, not of the admission, hostel or examination fees. B.Tech: AAT rank 1 to 100 receives a 50 percent tuition waiver, rank 101 to 500 receives 25 percent. BBA, B.Com and BA: class twelve aggregate of 95 percent or above receives 30 percent, and 90 to 94.9 percent receives 15 percent. MBA: the top 10 on the merit list receive 25 percent. To keep the scholarship in later years, a student must have a CGPA of 7.5 or above at the end of each year and no backlogs; scholarships lost are not restored in later years. Need-based fee waivers of up to 40 percent are available for families with an annual income below ₹4,00,000, on documentary proof. A sibling concession of 10 percent of tuition is given to the second child while both siblings are enrolled. A student can receive only one scholarship or concession at a time, whichever is highest.

title: Merit scholarships for batches admitted before 2026
text: This scheme applies only to students admitted in 2025 or earlier; it does not apply to the 2026 batch, which has its own scheme. B.Tech: AAT rank 1 to 200 received a 50 percent tuition waiver, and rank 201 to 1,000 received 25 percent. BBA, B.Com and BA: class twelve aggregate of 92 percent or above received 30 percent. To keep the scholarship, students under this scheme need a CGPA of 8.0 or above at the end of each year, but a single backlog cleared in the next supplementary examination does not cancel the scholarship. Scholarships lost under this scheme can be restored once if the CGPA returns above 8.0 the following year. Need-based waivers under this scheme were capped at 30 percent for families with an annual income below ₹3,00,000. The sibling concession was 5 percent of tuition. Students under this scheme who are on scholarship continue under these rules until they graduate.

title: Withdrawal and refund policy, 2026 intake
text: A student who withdraws must submit the withdrawal form signed by the student and a parent, with the original fee receipt. Refunds are made to the bank account the fee was paid from, within 30 days of the withdrawal form. Tuition refunds depend on the date of withdrawal: before 31 July 2026, the full tuition paid is refunded minus a processing charge of ₹2,000; from 1 August to 31 August 2026, 50 percent of the tuition fee is refunded; from 1 September 2026, no tuition is refunded. The one-time admission fee of ₹25,000 is non-refundable in all cases, including withdrawal before classes start and cancellation because the student got a seat elsewhere. The hostel caution deposit is refunded in full after room handover; hostel and mess fees are refunded for complete unused months only. Original certificates are never kept by the university and are returned the same day the withdrawal form is accepted.

title: Hostel allotment and fees, 2026-27
text: Hostel rooms for first-year students are allotted after the first fee instalment is paid, in order of distance from home, starting with students from outside the state. Students whose permanent address is within 40 km of the campus are not eligible for a first-year hostel room. Fees for 2026-27 are ₹96,000 per year for a twin-sharing non-AC room and ₹1,18,000 per year for twin-sharing AC rooms, which are limited to second year and above. The mess is compulsory for all hostel residents and costs ₹42,000 per year. A refundable caution deposit of ₹10,000 is paid once. Hostel and mess fees are paid annually by 15 July. Since July 2024 all hostels, for women and men, follow the same 10 pm curfew; the gate re-opens at 5:30 am. Late entry needs a pass from the warden issued before 6 pm. Rooms come with a bed, mattress, study table, chair and cupboard; students bring their own bedding, bucket and lock.

title: Women's hostel rules (2022 handbook, superseded)
text: This page reproduces the women's hostel section of the 2022 hostel handbook, which was superseded in July 2024 when common rules were adopted for all hostels; it is kept for reference only. Under the 2022 rules, the women's hostel curfew was 8:30 pm on weekdays and 9 pm on weekends, while the men's hostel curfew was 10 pm. Night-out permission for women residents needed a written request from a parent sent to the warden at least 24 hours in advance. Visitors were allowed only in the reception area between 4 pm and 7 pm on Sundays. The fee for a twin-sharing room in the women's hostel was ₹88,000 per year and the mess cost ₹38,000 per year. Guests of residents could not stay overnight. Residents who broke the curfew three times in a semester were reported to their parents and could lose their room for the following year.

title: Documents for reporting day and provisional admission
text: On reporting day, admitted students bring originals and two sets of self-attested photocopies of: class ten and class twelve marksheets and certificates, the transfer certificate from the last institution, the migration certificate if the student studied under a board or university outside the state, the AAT scorecard where applicable, a government photo ID, six passport-size photographs, and a medical fitness certificate. Students claiming a reserved seat must produce a category certificate issued on or after 1 April 2025, even for categories where the certificate itself has no expiry. If the migration certificate is not ready, the student gets provisional admission and must submit it within 60 days of reporting, after which the provisional admission is cancelled and fees are refunded as per the refund policy. The anti-ragging undertaking by the student and a parent must be submitted online before reporting. Originals are checked and returned on the spot.

title: Lateral entry into B.Tech second year
text: Diploma holders in engineering can join the B.Tech programme directly in the second year (third semester) through lateral entry. Applicants need at least 55 percent in the diploma, or 50 percent for SC and ST candidates of the state, in a branch that matches or is allied to the B.Tech branch applied for. Lateral entry seats are supernumerary, equal to 10 percent of the intake of each branch, and are filled on diploma marks without the AAT. B.Sc graduates with Mathematics are also eligible for lateral entry, but only to the Computer Science and Civil branches. All lateral entry students must complete a bridge course in engineering mathematics during the third semester; the bridge course fee is ₹8,000, and the course must be passed before the fifth semester. Lateral entry students pay the yearly B.Tech tuition for three years and are eligible for need-based waivers but not merit scholarships.

title: Transfer from other universities and credit transfer
text: Students from other recognised universities can transfer into a matching programme only at the start of the third semester, and only when vacant seats exist in that branch. Mid-year transfers, including after the first semester, are not accepted. Applications for transfer close on 30 June each year. The student must have passed all first-year subjects with no backlogs and a CGPA of at least 6.5. A credit evaluation fee of ₹15,000 is charged, and it is not refunded if the transfer is refused. A maximum of 40 percent of the total credits of the degree can be transferred from the previous university; any remaining first-year courses that do not map to ours must be completed as additional courses without extra fee. The degree is awarded by this university, and the transcript lists transferred credits as such, without grades. Transfer students are not eligible for merit scholarships in their first year here.

title: Admissions office hours and campus visits
text: The admissions office in the Administrative Block is open from 9:30 am to 5 pm, Monday to Saturday. During the counselling weeks from 1 April to 31 July, it is also open on Sundays from 10 am to 2 pm for walk-in enquiries and document verification. Guided campus tours run at 11 am and 3 pm on working days and must be booked at least one day in advance by phone; Sunday visitors can see the campus but there are no guided tours on Sundays. The admissions helpline is open from 9 am to 7 pm daily during counselling weeks and from 9:30 am to 5 pm otherwise. Visitors' vehicles are parked at Gate 2; private vehicles are not allowed inside the academic zone. Parents attending counselling should bring the student's original documents and two sets of photocopies. The university information centre at the Meerapur railway station is open on weekdays only.
